title: Physical communication: pros & cons
blurb: Recognise physical (tangible, printed) communication and outline its advantages and disadvantages with confidence.
question: A school rebuild project writes to every neighbouring household about six weeks of piling works. Which advantages does a printed letter give the project, and which disadvantages should the project manager plan around?

teach.body: Physical communication is tangible: something people can hold, read on paper or see in a fixed place. Examples: printed reports, letters, contracts, posters, notice boards, newsletters, printed drawings and physical models or prototypes. In plain English: if it exists as an object rather than on a screen or in a conversation, it is physical.

teach.h: The main kinds of physical communication

teach.body: Physical communication gives a permanent record and an audit trail. It can be carefully drafted, checked and approved before it goes out, so it suits detailed, formal information. Readers can re-read it and refer back. One poster or newsletter reaches many people, and it does not depend on technology, so it works for people without email or on sites with no signal. A model lets people see and handle a design.

teach.body: Amira's team posts the site safety rules on the notice board at the gate, writes to 150 neighbouring homes about piling works, and places a model of the new school in reception for parents. The letters give a lasting record and reach residents with no email. But they take five days to print and deliver, two neighbours phone to complain the tone sounded dismissive, and when the piling dates move, the letter is out of date and has to be reissued.

teach.h: Why a letter is slow, and one-way

steps.label: Deliver
steps.sub: Post or hand delivery takes days

teach.caption: The first two steps are an advantage (considered and checked). The last four are where the disadvantages bite.

teach.text: Physical communication does NOT give immediate feedback, and it does NOT rely on technology. Exam options often swap these: 'relies on technology being available' is a virtual disadvantage, and 'allows instant clarification' is a face-to-face advantage. Its weakness is speed and one-way flow; its strength is the lasting record.

items: Physical = tangible or printed: reports, letters, posters, notice boards, newsletters, models.
Advantages: permanent record and audit trail, checked before sending, can be re-read, reaches many, suits formal detail, no technology needed.
Disadvantages: slow, no immediate feedback, tone misread, may not be read, print and distribution cost, goes out of date, environmental impact.
Exam tip: no instant feedback and no reliance on technology.

summary: You can now recognise physical communication and outline its advantages (lasting record, considered content, re-readable, wide reach, no technology needed) and disadvantages (slow, one-way, misread tone, unread, costly, out of date, environmental impact).

A.q: Which is an advantage of a printed progress report over a phone call?
options: It can be re-read and referred to later
It allows questions to be answered live
It conveys tone of voice more accurately
It is quicker to produce and to deliver
A.why: A printed report stays available, so readers can return to it and check details whenever they need to.

whyNot.1: Live questions and answers happen on the call, not with a printed report.
whyNot.2: A report carries no tone of voice; the phone call does.
whyNot.3: Printing and delivering a report is slower than making a call.

A.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of physical communication?
options: It leaves no record for later audit
It depends on reliable internet access
Readers cannot give immediate feedback
It cannot be checked before it is sent
A.why: Physical communication is one-way at the point of reading: a reader with a question cannot get an instant answer.

whyNot.0: A lasting record is one of physical communication's main advantages.
whyNot.1: Physical methods do not need the internet; that is a virtual disadvantage.
whyNot.3: Being drafted and checked before sending is an advantage of physical communication.

A.q: Which of the following is an example of physical communication?
options: A video walkthrough of the design
A site tour led by the architect
A shared online planning board
A scale model of the new building
A.why: A scale model is a tangible object people can see and handle, so it is physical communication.

whyNot.0: A video walkthrough is delivered through technology, so it is virtual.
whyNot.1: A tour led in person is face to face.
whyNot.2: An online board is a virtual collaboration tool.

B.q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of sending a formal letter?
options: It can be approved before it is sent
It gives instant answers to questions
It reaches people who have no email
It provides lasting evidence of content
B.why: A letter is one-way when it is read: the reader cannot get an instant answer to a question. Instant clarification is a face-to-face strength.

whyNot.0: Letters can be drafted, checked and approved first, which is an advantage.
whyNot.2: Not depending on technology is an advantage of physical methods.
whyNot.3: A letter is a permanent record, an advantage.

B.q: A project prints a monthly newsletter. Two days after it is printed, the opening date of the new facility moves. Which disadvantage of physical communication does this show?
options: It relies on staff having devices
It is too informal for important news
It can quickly become out of date
It cannot reach large audiences
B.why: Once printed, physical communication is fixed. When plans change it goes out of date and must be reprinted or corrected.

whyNot.0: Needing devices is a virtual disadvantage; print needs none.
whyNot.1: Newsletters can carry formal news; the problem here is timing.
whyNot.3: A newsletter can reach many people; reach is an advantage.

B.q: Why is a printed, signed document well suited to recording a contract change?
options: It creates a lasting audit trail
It gives faster agreement on terms
It removes the need to negotiate
It lets both sides edit it freely
B.why: A signed physical document is permanent evidence of what was agreed, which is exactly what an audit trail needs.

whyNot.1: Printing, signing and posting is slower than most other methods.
whyNot.2: Negotiation still happens; the document records its outcome.
whyNot.3: Free editing would undermine the record; a signed document is fixed.

C.q: Which TWO are advantages of physical communication? 1) It can be re-read. 2) It gives instant feedback. 3) It does not depend on technology. 4) It is the cheapest way to reach a dispersed team.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
C.why: Physical communication can be re-read and does not need technology to be received.

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: physical communication gives no instant feedback.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: no instant feedback, and printing and posting to a dispersed team costs more than virtual methods.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: virtual methods are usually cheaper for a dispersed team.

C.q: A project manager sends a firmly worded letter to a supplier about late deliveries. The supplier takes offence and the relationship cools. Which disadvantage of physical communication is shown?
options: Tone can be misread and not clarified
It is too costly to print a single letter
It depends on the supplier having a printer
It leaves no evidence of what was said
C.why: Written words lack tone and body language, and the reader cannot ask what was meant, so a firm tone can be read as hostile.

whyNot.1: The cost of one letter is trivial; the problem was how it was read.
whyNot.2: The letter arrived on paper; no technology was needed.
whyNot.3: A letter is a lasting record, so there is clear evidence of what was said.

C.q: A remote quarry site has no mobile signal and most workers have no company email. What is the most effective way to tell everyone about a new evacuation route?
options: A group email to everyone on the site team
A message on the project intranet
A video briefing to watch online
Posters at entrances and in the canteen
C.why: Physical posters do not depend on technology and are seen by everyone who passes them, which suits this audience.

whyNot.0: Most workers have no company email, so they would not receive it.
whyNot.1: An intranet needs network access and accounts the workers lack.
whyNot.2: Watching online needs a signal and devices the site does not have.

reteach.title: The village fete poster
reteach.question: A village committee advertises its summer fete with posters in the shop, the pub and on the church notice board. What does the poster do well, and where does it let them down?

blocks.body: Everyone who walks past sees it, including people who never go online. It was checked by the committee before printing, and it stays up for weeks. But people who don't pass the pub never see it, nobody can ask it whether dogs are allowed, and when the date moves because of rain, every poster is wrong until someone reprints them.

rows.label: Reach
values: Missed by those who never pass

blocks.text: Projects work the same way: physical communication is lasting and needs no technology, but it is one-way and slow to update.

explain.body: Physical communication is tangible: printed reports, letters, posters, notice boards, newsletters and physical models or prototypes. If it travels through a screen it is virtual; if it happens in person it is face to face.

test.q: Which of the following is NOT physical communication?
options: A printed project newsletter
An instant message to the team
A notice in the site canteen
A prototype handed to users
test.why: An instant message is sent through technology, so it is virtual communication.

whyNot.0: A printed newsletter is tangible, so it is physical.
whyNot.2: A notice displayed in a fixed place is physical.
whyNot.3: A prototype people can handle is physical.

explain.body: Because physical communication is drafted before it is sent, it can be checked and approved. Once issued, it stays: readers can return to it, and it forms part of the audit trail.

test.q: A formal board report is reviewed by the sponsor before being printed and issued. Which advantage of physical communication does this show?
options: It reaches people without any technology
It allows immediate two-way discussion
It is quick to update when plans change
Its content is checked before it is sent
test.why: Physical communication can be considered, reviewed and approved before release, which suits formal content such as board reports.

whyNot.0: That is a real advantage, but it is not what the sponsor's review shows.
whyNot.1: A printed report is one-way; discussion needs a meeting or call.
whyNot.2: Printed documents are slow to update; that is a disadvantage.

explain.body: One poster or newsletter reaches everyone who sees it, with no devices needed. Models and prototypes go further: stakeholders can see and handle a design, which drawings or emails cannot match.

items.label: works without email, devices or signal
a single poster is seen by all who pass
models and prototypes can be handled

test.q: Which advantage does a physical prototype offer stakeholders reviewing a new product?
options: They can see and handle the design
It updates itself as the design changes
It sends their comments to the designers
It costs nothing to produce or change
test.why: A prototype is tangible, so stakeholders can try it out, which helps them understand and give useful comments.

whyNot.1: A physical prototype is fixed; it must be rebuilt to reflect changes.
whyNot.2: A prototype cannot transmit comments; feedback needs another channel.
whyNot.3: Prototypes can be costly to make and to change.

explain.body: Physical communication is slow to produce and distribute, gives no immediate feedback, can have its tone misread, may not be read, costs money to print and deliver, goes out of date and has an environmental impact.

test.q: Which is a disadvantage of a printed newsletter sent to 500 stakeholders?
options: It leaves no record of what was said
It needs every reader to have a device
It adds printing and distribution cost
It gives too much immediate feedback
test.why: Printing and delivering 500 copies costs money (and paper), a recognised disadvantage of physical methods.

whyNot.0: A newsletter is a lasting record.
whyNot.1: Printed copies need no device; that is a virtual drawback.
whyNot.3: Physical communication gives little or no immediate feedback.
